DAY-01.note: GK bank fact card for subtopic 'january' (db/gk/important_days.jsonl). All eight dates it lists are taught in this chapter: 9 Jan Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (pravasi_youth), 12 Jan Youth Day (pravasi_youth), 15 Jan Army Day (army_parakram), 23 Jan Parakram Diwas (army_parakram), 24 Jan Girl Child Day (girl_child), 25 Jan Voters' Day + Tourism Day (voters_tourism), 26 Jan Republic Day (republic_day), 30 Jan Martyrs' Day (martyrs_day). Its three bank questions (Voters' Day date, Youth Day person, January pairs) are fully covered. One sub-detail is NOT claim-backed in this draft: the card gives 1948 as the year of Gandhi's assassination; the fetched PIB/PMO pages used here state the date and the death-anniversary reason but do not print the year, so the year is not taught (see the Clerkship 2019 entry below).

'The Constitution of India came into force on' — 26.01.1950. Taught in republic_day with the adoption-vs-enforcement distinction (adopted 26 Nov 1949), claim c23 from the PIB Constitution Day factsheet.

Asks the YEAR of Gandhi's assassination on 30 January (answer 1948). This chapter teaches the date, the Punya Tithi / death-anniversary reason, Rajghat homage and the 11 AM two-minute silence from fetched PIB/PMO pages (claims c29, c30), but none of the fetched official pages prints the year 1948, so the year itself is not taught in this draft. Source gap, disclosed in the chapter text and REPORT.md.

Asks who was chief guest at the Republic Day parade in 2008 (Nicolas Sarkozy). A year-specific chief guest is current-affairs material; this chapter teaches only the permanent date and reason of Republic Day (Constitution in force, 26 Jan 1950). Not taught, by design.

Asks who was Chief Guest of Republic Day 2021 (answer: none of them — no foreign chief guest that year). Year-specific chief-guest/current-affairs item; the chapter teaches the permanent date and reason only. Not taught, by design.
